entities.name: Murrow's Shard

fields.note: Murrow's own tool, combined from six auto mode ideas
fields.where: Monstradius. Murrow keeps it on him in his coat pocket while he works, and locks it in a warded alcove in the workshop wall at night.
fields.does: Senses traces of magic. Held near a person, tool or place, it pulses warm and faintly lights up, showing thin, coloured "threads" where mana has been used recently: what kind and how strong, never who. Murrow uses it to diagnose broken enchanted items, spot anyone copying an artificer's work, and check whether someone is quietly drawing on mana. Held close to a spell as it's cast, it can briefly amplify it (a gust reaches twice as far, a healer's touch runs stronger) for a few seconds.
fields.made: A smooth, robin's-egg-sized shard of mirrorstone, etched with fine silver lines. It was part of an unfinished Rift compass belonging to Silas Brightstone, the travelling artificer Murrow apprenticed under long ago. Silas vanished while working on it near the Ashen Reach when a small rift tore open; the surge overloaded the mirrorstone and left this shard behind, and Murrow salvaged it.
fields.limits: Uses the holder's own mana, never stored mana, and it can't be charged. Range is about 10 feet, up to 30 at most, shrinking with heavy use. It only shows active or recent magic: old, faded magic and steady wards barely register, and strong elemental or divine magic drowns it out. Amplifying lasts seconds and costs about a full day's exertion. Overuse brings dizziness, chills (the shard turns painfully cold as the holder runs low), headaches, gaps in memory and brief "echoes" of other artificers' thoughts. Forcing it without an attuned mind causes painful backlash. Elves and those attuned to elemental magic find it easier to use.
fields.story: It's the heart of Murrow's study of rifts and of the Rift compass, and of his hope to store mana in objects. He believes it holds an echo of the rift that made it, and that it might one day open small, controlled rifts, though it never has. Doric is the only one allowed to examine it, and has tried and failed to copy it. Clementine Rook has been shown it a few times under strict supervision. Murrow won't say what it does.

entities.name: Embercrown

fields.does: A delicate metal crown set with gems that glow like embers, worn by the Kingdom's royals at official events in the capital. Worn outside formal occasions, it stirs whispers of court gossip and intrigue around the wearer.
fields.made: Needs rare materials to craft. The ember glow is a fire user's mana stored in the gems, so like every enchanted item it runs dry and has to be charged again.
fields.limits: Royals only, and only for ceremonies. The edge of the realm never sees it, and most of the capital only ever sees the Crown's banner.
fields.story: Raises how much influence and authority people see in the wearer. Who charges it is a question for the register of artificers. Open question: where is it kept when it isn't worn? The Crown's seat beside the Rolls House is the obvious guess.
